title: Initial Data & Placeholder Data
description: Learn how to use initialData and placeholderData to provide instant UI feedback during data fetches.

data.text: React Query provides two powerful options to improve perceived performance: **initialData** and **placeholderData**. Both let you show something before the network request completes, but they work in very different ways.

**initialData** is a synchronous value used only on the very first render when no cached data exists yet. It lets the UI display data immediately instead of waiting for the first network response. Once the query completes, React Query replaces initialData with the real server response â€” and subsequent renders use the cache.

data.title: initialData is One-Time
data.text: initialData is consumed only on the first render. After the query succeeds, the cache takes over. If you navigate away and back, the cache is used â€” not initialData.

**placeholderData** is used whenever cached data is missing or stale. Unlike initialData, it can be applied on every render where the cache is empty. It accepts either a static value or a function that returns the previous page's data â€” making it ideal for smooth pagination transitions.

data.content: Providing initial data so the UI never shows an empty state

data.text: placeholderData shines in pagination. When the user clicks "Next", React Query fetches page 2. While that request is in flight, page 1 data remains visible â€” so the UI never feels broken. The data shown during the fetch is considered "placeholder" and not yet committed to the cache.

cards.title: initialData
cards.description: A static or computed value shown only on the very first render when the cache is empty.
pros: Great for SSR or pre-fetched data
cons: Only used once â€” on first render
Stale if the data changes before the response arrives
Can give a false sense of freshness

cards.title: placeholderData
cards.description: A fallback value (static or function) used whenever the cache is missing data. Can be reapplied on every relevant render.
pros: Used every time data is missing from cache
Can derive from previous page data via function
cons: Data is not committed to the cache
Requires careful type handling for pagination

data.title: Use initialData when:
items: You have pre-loaded data from SSR or a parent route loader
You want to seed the cache from localStorage on first visit
You want the UI to feel instant on first mount and don't care about slight staleness
You pass data from a parent component that already fetched it

data.title: Use placeholderData when:
items: You want a smooth UX during pagination or infinite scroll
You need to show stale data while a refetch completes
You want a fallback for any cache miss, not just the first render
The user navigates between views that share query keys

terms.definition: A static or computed value provided to useQuery that is used only on the first render when no cached data exists. Acts as a synchronous stand-in for the upcoming network response.

A fallback value (static or function) used by useQuery whenever the cache is empty. Unlike initialData, it can be reapplied on every render where data is missing, including during pagination transitions.
A special placeholderData value that returns the previous query's data. Used to keep the UI populated while a new page loads during pagination.
A caching strategy where stale (outdated) data is served immediately to the user while a background refetch updates the cache with fresh data. React Query implements this by default.

data.text: You can use both options in the same query. initialData seeds the first render, and placeholderData covers subsequent renders where data might have been garbage-collected. This gives you instant loading on first visit and smooth transitions throughout the session.

data.content: Using both options together for the best UX

data.title: Type Safety with placeholderData
data.text: When using a function with placeholderData, TypeScript may require a type assertion. Use a type guard or cast carefully: placeholderData: (prev) => prev as Article[] | undefined

data.title: Build a Search with instantFeedback
data.description: Create a search component that fetches results from a mock API. Use initialData to show previous search results instantly when the component mounts. Then add placeholderData so that if the user clears the search and starts typing again, old results remain visible while the new request is in flight.
steps: Create a useQuery that fetches results from /api/search?q={query}
Set initialData to [] so the component never renders an empty list on first load
Set placeholderData to keepPreviousData for smooth search transitions
Display a 'Searching...' badge when isPlaceholderData is true
Log to the console when initialData is used vs when real data arrives
data.expectedOutcome: A search component that feels instant: old results persist during new searches, and the first mount never shows an empty state. The console shows clear logs for initialData consumption vs cache hits.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: initialData is used only on the first render when the cache is empty
placeholderData is used every time cached data is missing or stale
Use initialData for SSR data, localStorage seeds, or parent-provided props
Use placeholderData for pagination, search transitions, and cache-rebuilding scenarios
Both options dramatically improve perceived performance without extra network requests
Combining both gives the best UX across the full query lifecycle
data.takeaway: initialData seeds the first impression; placeholderData keeps it smooth throughout the session.

data.title: Initial Data & Placeholder Data â€” FAQ

items.question: Does initialData trigger a network request?
items.answer: No. initialData is a local value â€” it does not trigger any fetch. The network request still fires normally; React Query simply shows initialData in the UI while waiting.

items.question: Will placeholderData overwrite my cache?
items.answer: No. placeholderData is never written to the cache. It is only used for rendering. The real response is committed to the cache when it arrives.

items.question: Can I use a function for initialData?
items.answer: Yes. initialData accepts a function that is called synchronously on the first render. This is useful for reading from localStorage or extracting data from window.__NEXT_DATA__ in SSR apps.

items.question: What happens if initialData throws an error?
items.answer: If the initialData function throws, React Query falls back to the normal loading state. Wrap your logic in try/catch to be safe.

items.question: How is this different from stale-while-revalidate?
items.answer: stale-while-revalidate is the overall caching strategy React Query uses. initialData and placeholderData are tools within that strategy: they provide the data that gets shown to the user while the revalidation request completes in the background.
